IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p294#2/r4.anchor: أسند الطبري إلى خباب بن الأرت أن الأقرع بن حابس ومن شابهه من أشراف العرب قالوا للنبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r1.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r1.claim: Al-Mahdawi says all the pronouns in the passage refer to the believers; Hasan says their accounting concerns their deeds, as most interpreters hold.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r1.anchor: فعلى هذا تجيء الضمائر كلها للمؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r2.claim: The first min is partitive and the second is emphatic; the two fa-verbs follow the prior negation and prohibition, and being among wrongdoers means putting things in the wrong place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p296/r2.anchor: ومن الأولى للتبعيض والثانية زائدة مؤكدة

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r1.claim: The apparent reading returns all three pronouns to one group: those who call upon their Lord.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r1.anchor: والضمائر الثلاثة، أعني التي في قوله: { من حسابهم }

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r2.speaker: الطبري
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r2.claim: Al-Tabari also takes all three pronouns as referring to the worshippers, but understands their account as worldly provision.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r2.anchor: وهم الذين يدعون ربهم، وبه قال الطبري، إلا أنه فسر الحساب بالرزق الدنيوي

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r3.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya refer the first two pronouns to the polytheists and the third to the worshippers.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري وبان عطية: " إن الضميرين الأولين يعودان على المشركين

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r4.claim: Another view refers the pronouns in their account and upon them to the polytheists, making the two clauses parenthetical.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r4.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في " حسابهم " و " عليهم " عائد على المشركين وتكون الجملتان اعتراضا

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r5.claim: The two clauses can be parenthetical regardless of whom the first two pronouns refer to; they interrupt the prohibition and its result.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#5/r5.anchor: بل هما اعتراض بين النهي وهو " لا تطرد " وبين جوابه وهو فتكون

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r1.claim: The subjunctive فتطردهم can answer the prohibition or express the consequence of the negated mutual accounting; the intended sense denies both expulsion and its cause.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r1.anchor: ما يكون مؤاخذة كل واحد بحساب صاحبه فيكف يقع طرد؟

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r2.claim: The alternative reading of the example, where the visit occurs but the conversation does not, does not suit this verse.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r2.anchor: وهذا المعنى لا يليق بالآية الكريمة

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r3.claim: فتكون is most clearly coordinated with فتطردهم, reporting expulsion and the injustice that results from it.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r3.anchor: أظهرهما: أنه منصوب عطفا على " فتطردهم " والمعنى:

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows coordination, treating being unjust as caused by expelling them.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r4.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن تكون عطفا على " فتطردهم "

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r5.speaker: مكي والواحدي وأبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r5.claim: Makki, al-Wahidi, and Abu al-Baqa mention فتكون as a response to the prohibition.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r5.anchor: ولم يذكر مكي ولا الواحدي ولا أبو البقاء غيره

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan compares this construction with the prohibition in Ta-Ha 20:61 and treats the intervening clauses as parenthetical.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r6.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وجوزوا أن يكون " فتكون " جوابا

SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r7.claim: The parenthetical analysis does not depend on referring the first two pronouns to the polytheists.
SAMIN-DURR:6:52#6/r7.anchor: قلت: قد تقدم أن كونهما اعتراضا لا يتوقف على عود الضميرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r1.claim: The verse concerned six poor Companions, including Sa'd, Ibn Masud, Suhayb, Ammar, al-Miqdad, and Bilal; Quraysh demanded the Prophet expel them rather than be seen following them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r1.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في ستة في وفي ابن مسعود وصهيب وعمار والمقداد وبلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r2.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r2.claim: Khabbab says poor believers learned from the Prophet morning and evening; al-Aqra and Uyayna demanded they be removed, then pressed for a written agreement, until Gabriel brought the warning against expelling them and the Prophet welcomed them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r2.anchor: كنا ضعفاء عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلمنا بالغداة والعشي ما ينفعنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r3.claim: Quraysh leaders passing by the Prophet and poor Companions asked whether he expected them to become followers of those men.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r3.anchor: مر الملأ من قريش على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده خباب وصهيب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r4.claim: Nobles of Abd Manaf asked Abu Talib to make Muhammad expel clients and slaves; Umar suggested trying it, but the verse came and Umar apologized.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r4.anchor: فقالوا لو أن ابن أخيك يطرد عنه موالينا وعبيدنا كان أعظم في صدورنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r5.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r5.claim: The verse concerns the clients Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Ammar, Mihja, Salman, Amir ibn Fuhayra, and Salim, and another verse also addressed them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r5.anchor: أن هذه الآيات نزلت في الموالي منهم بلال وصهيب وخباب وعمار ومهجع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r6.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r6.claim: Some nobles offered belief if the Prophet delayed the poor believers and let them pray behind the nobles; this report seeks moving them from the prayer row, unlike the others' request to remove them from his gathering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p44/r6.anchor: نؤمن لك وإذا صلينا فأخر هؤلاء الذين معك فليصلوا خلفنا فعلى هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r1.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r1.claim: Calling upon their Lord means the obligatory prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r1.anchor: أنه الصلاة المكتوبة قاله ابن عمر وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as the five daily prayers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r3.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r3.claim: Another report from Mujahid and Qatada identifies the prayers as dawn and afternoon.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r3.anchor: وفي رواية عن مجاهد وقتادة قالا يعني صلاة الصبح والعصر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r4.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r4.claim: Muqatil says prayer at that time was two units at dawn and two at evening, before the five daily prayers were prescribed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r4.anchor: وزعم مقاتل أن الصلاة يومئذ كانت ركعتين بالغداة وركعتين بالعشي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r5.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r5.claim: Another interpretation of calling on God is remembering Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه ذكر الله تعالى قاله إبراهيم النخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r6.anchor: والثالث أنه عبادة الله قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r7.claim: Another interpretation is learning the Qur'an morning and evening.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r7.anchor: والرابع أنه تعلم القرآن غدوة وعشية قاله أبو جعفر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r8.claim: Another interpretation is praying to God with monotheism, sincerity, and worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r8.anchor: والخامس أنه دعاء الله بالتوحيد والإخلاص له وعبادته قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r9.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r9.claim: Most readers say bil-ghadah; Ibn Amir reads bil-ghudwah here and in al-Kahf 18:28. Farra sees ghudwah as inherently definite, Abu Ali says ghadah can take the article while ghudwah is a proper name, and al-Khalil permits it as a time word like duha.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر هاهنا وفي الكهف أيضا بالغدوة بضم الغين وإسكان الدال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r10.claim: Morning stands for the whole day and evening for the night; if a person's daytime worship is sincere, nighttime worship is even purer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p46/r10.anchor: نبه بالغداة على جميع النهار وبالعشي على الليل لأنه إذا كان عمل النهار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r1.claim: Those who seek God's face seek God Himself, and God attests to the sincerity of their intentions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r1.anchor: أي يريدون الله فيشهد الله لهم بصحة النيات وأنهم مخلصون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r2.claim: The account mentioned here is an account of deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r2.anchor: أحدها أنه حساب الأعمال قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r3.claim: Other interpretations of the account mentioned are provision or sufficiency: neither group is responsible for providing for the other.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r3.anchor: والثالث أنه بمعنى الكفاية والمعنى ما عليك من كفايتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r4.claim: The warning not to expel them threatens inclusion among the wrongdoers because the Prophet had considered giving the leaders precedence over the weak.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p47/r4.anchor: عظم هذا الأمر على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وخوف بالدخول في جملة الظالمين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259/r2.claim: Do not drive away people who invoke God morning and evening seeking His face; keep them close as companions, as also commanded in 18:28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259/r2.anchor: أي: لا تبعد هؤلاء المتصفين بهذه الصفة عنك، بل اجعلهم جلساءك وأخصاءك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب ومجاهد والحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatada say the morning and evening invocation refers to the obligatory prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب، ومجاهد، والحسن، وقتادة: المراد بذلك الصلوات المكتوبات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r2.claim: Invoking God means worshipping and asking Him; 40:60 similarly says to call upon God and He will respond.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r2.anchor: وقوله {يدعون ربهم} أي: يعبدونه ويسألونه {بالغداة والعشي}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r3.claim: Seeking God’s face means that these worshippers sincerely seek His favor through their worship and obedience.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r3.anchor: وقوله: {يريدون وجهه} أي: يبتغون بذلك العمل وجه الله الكريم، فهم مخلصون فيما هم فيه من العبادات والطاعات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r4.claim: Neither the Prophet nor these worshippers answer for one another; Ibn Kathir compares Noah’s response that their account belongs to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#2/r4.anchor: أي: إنما حسابهم على الله، عز وجل، وليس علي من حسابهم من شيء، كما أنه ليس عليهم من حسابي من شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r1.claim: Seeking God’s face means that these people sincerely seek His favor through their worship and obedience.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r1.anchor: وقوله: {فتطردهم فتكون من الظالمين} أي: إن فعلت هذا والحالة هذه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r2.claim: Neither the Prophet nor these worshippers answer for one another; Ibn Kathir compares Noah’s response that their account belongs to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r2.anchor: قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا أسباط -هو ابن محمد -حدثنا أشعث، عن كردوس، عن ابن مسعود قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r3.speaker: خباب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r3.claim: Khabbab says al-Aqra and Uyayna disdained the poor believers and sought an exclusive meeting with the Prophet; Gabriel revealed the command not to expel them, and the Prophet discarded their written pledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p259#3/r3.anchor: عن خباب في قول الله، عز وجل: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي} قال: جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r1.claim: Al-Hakim grades Sa’d’s report about six Companions according to the criteria of al-Bukhari and Muslim; Ibn Hibban also transmits its route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r1.anchor: رواه الحاكم في مستدركه من طريق سفيان، وقال: على شرط الشيخين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says Ibn Jarir also transmits the earlier report through Asbat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r2.anchor: ورواه ابن جرير، من حديث أسباط، به. (7)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report strange because this verse is Meccan whereas al-Aqra and Uyayna converted long after the Hijra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r3.anchor: وهذا حديث غريب، فإن هذه الآية مكية، والأقرع بن حابس وعيينة إنما أسلما بعد الهجرة بدهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r4.speaker: سعد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r4.claim: Sa’d says the verse concerned six Companions, including Ibn Masud, who arrived early and drew near to hear the Prophet; Quraysh objected to their proximity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p260/r4.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في ستة من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، منهم ابن مسعود

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads بالغدوة والعشي with wāw and a ḍamma on ghayn in both this verse and al-Kahf; the other readers have alif and fatḥa.
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر: بالغدوة والعشي بالواو وضم الغين، وفي سورة (الكهف) مثله

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the plural forms بالغدوات والعشيات; the original wāw turns into alif after fatḥa on the preceding dāl.
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: بالغدوات والعشيات وأصله الواو، ولذلك يجمع غدوات

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r3.claim: Ṭard means banishing, exclusion, or expulsion.
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r3.anchor: الطرد والإقصاء والتشريد نظائر، وهو الإبعاد

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r4.claim: Wajh can mean the familiar bodily face or the essence/aspect of a thing, as in saying this is the wajh of an opinion.
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r4.anchor: والوجه: الجارحة المعروفة، سميت بذلك لأنها تواجهك، والوجه: نفس الشيء أيضا

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r7.claim: The prohibition طرد is jussive, with kasra to separate adjacent vowelless consonants; فتطردهم can answer the negation in ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء.
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r7.anchor: ولا تطرد جزم للنهي، وكسر لالتقاء الساكنين. فتطردهم جواب للجحود

JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r8.claim: Abū Muslim parses فتطردهم فتكون as consequences of the prohibition: do not expel them, or you become unjust by expelling them.
JISHUMI:v3p2244#2/r8.anchor: عن أبي مسلم. والكاف في قوله: وكذلك كاف التشبيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r1.claim: After warning those Muslims who are not yet devout, the text turns to the devout: draw them near and honor them, and do not obey those seeking the opposite.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r1.anchor: ثم أردفهم ذكر المتقين منهم وأمره بتقريبهم وإكرامهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r2.claim: Calling on their Lord morning and evening means continuous worship; alternatively it specifically means the dawn and afternoon prayers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه : يصلون صلاة الصبح والعصر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r3.claim: Seeking God's face denotes sincerity; ‘face’ can express a thing's essence and reality.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r4.speaker: رؤسا من المشركين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r4.claim: Polytheist leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor believers such as Ammar, Suhayb, Bilal, Khabbab, and Salman so they could speak with him; he refused, then briefly considered their request in hope they might believe, before revelation forbade it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r4.anchor: لو طردت عنا هؤلاء الأعبد يعنون فقراء المسلمين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r5.speaker: سلمان وخباب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r5.claim: Salman and Khabbab say this was revealed about them: the Prophet sat very close, then revelation told him to remain with them until they rose; he praised God for living to receive that command.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r5.anchor: قال سلمان وخباب : فينا نزلت فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r6.claim: The accounting clauses assure the Prophet that allegations about the believers do not bind him: he judges outward signs, and any hidden fault remains their burden, as in the rule that no bearer bears another's burden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r6.anchor: فما يلزمك إلا اعتبار الظاهر والاتسام بسيمة المتقين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r7.claim: Both accounting clauses are needed together to convey that neither group is answerable for the other's account.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r7.anchor: ولا يستقل بهذا المعنى إلا الجملتان جميعا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r8.claim: Another view takes the pronouns to refer to the polytheists: they are not responsible for the Prophet's account nor he for theirs, so eagerness for their conversion must not lead him to expel believers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r8.anchor: لا يؤاخذون بحسابك ولا أنت بحسابهم ، حتى يهمك إيمانهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r9.claim: In the syntax, فتطردهم responds to the negation and فتكون to the prohibition; alternatively, it coordinates as a consequence because injustice results from expelling them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p26#3/r9.anchor: جواب النهي . ويجوز أن يكون عطفا على

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r5.claim: Quraysh leaders asked Muhammad to expel weak believers including Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, and Ibn Masud, promising to follow if he did; Umar urged a trial, and the Prophet considered it before the verse came down.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r5.anchor: يا محمد اطرد عنا موالينا وحلفاءنا فإنما هم عبيدنا وعتقاؤنا , فلعلك إن طردتهم نتبعك

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid interpret those calling on their Lord morning and evening as performing the five prayers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r7.anchor: أنها الصلوات الخمس , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r8.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r8.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai interprets calling on their Lord as remembrance of God; other views say Qur'an recitation or worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r8.anchor: والثاني : أنه ذكر الله , قاله إبراهيم النخعي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r9.claim: Abu Jafar interprets the devotional calling as honoring the Qur'an; al-Dahhak says it is worship of God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r9.anchor: والثالث : تعظيم القرآن , قاله أبو جعفر . والرابع : أنه عبادة الله , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r10.claim: Seeking God's face may mean intending Him, since Arabic uses face for the thing itself to magnify it, or seeking His obedience by aiming toward what He directs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r10.anchor: معنى قوله : { يريدون وجهه } فيه قولان : أحدهما : يريدون بدعائهم , لأن العرب تذكر وجه الشيء إرادة له

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r11.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says each person answers for their own deeds, so neither group bears the other's reward or punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r11.anchor: أحدها : يعني ما عليك من حساب عملهم من شيء من ثواب أو عقاب . { وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء }

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r12.speaker: ابن بحر
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r12.claim: Ibn Bahr interprets reckoning as provision: neither group is responsible for maintaining the other, since his reading of 78:36 describes a complete, sufficient gift.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p116/r12.anchor: والثالث : ما عليك كفايتهم ولا عليهم كفايتك , والحساب الكفاية كقوله تعالى : ^ { عطاء حسابا } ^ [ النبأ : 36 ]

MUJAHID:v1p215#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p215#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p215#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the people who pray at dawn and evening as worshippers Bilal and Ibn Umm Ma'bad, who sat with the Prophet; Quraysh said they would join him if not for such low-status companions, so the Prophet was forbidden to expel them.
MUJAHID:v1p215#3/r1.anchor: يعني المصلين بلالا وابن أم معبد كانا يجالسان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت قريش محقرتهما

MUQATIL:6:52-54/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r1.claim: Abu Talib suggested Muhammad dismiss his poor followers so the nobles might follow him, but the verse forbade turning away those who pray for God.
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r1.anchor: قال أبو طالب للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: لو طردت هؤلاء عنك، لعل سراة قومك يتبعونك،

MUQATIL:6:52-54/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r2.claim: The dawn and evening prayers were then two units each; the five daily prayers were prescribed later.
MUQATIL:6:52-54/r2.anchor: قال: وكانت الصلاة يومئذ ركعتين بالغداة وركعتين بالعشى، ثم فرضت الصلوات الخمس بعد ذلك.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r1.claim: After commanding warning of the non-pious, God commands drawing the pious near and forbids their dismissal.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r1.anchor: ولما أمر النبى عليه السلام بإنذار غير المتقين ليتقوا أمر بعد ذلك بتقريب المتقين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r2.claim: Calling on God morning and evening means continuous worship, or specifically dawn and afternoon prayers, or all five prayers; the Shami reading has the stated form of 'morning.'
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r2.anchor: أى عبادته ويواظبون عليها والمراد بذكر الغداة والعشى الدوام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r3.claim: Seeking God's face means sincerity; 'face' can denote a thing's essence and reality.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r3.anchor: ووسمهم بالإخلاص فى عبادتهم بقوله ﴿ يريدون وجهه ﴾ فالوجه يعبر به عن ذات الشئ

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r4.claim: Revelation followed the chiefs' demand to dismiss poor believers Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar, and others; the Prophet refused, they requested alternate days and a written agreement, then the poor moved aside as Ali was called to write. The Prophet threw away the paper and embraced them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r4.anchor: نزلت فى الفقراء بلال وصهيب وعمار وأضرابهم حين قال رؤساء المشركين لو طردت هؤلاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r5.claim: The believers' account is theirs alone and cannot transfer to the Prophet; the source compares the statement with a verse about Noah's reckoning.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r5.anchor: حسباهم عليهم لازم لهم لا يتعداهم اليك كما أن حسابك عليك لا يتعداك اليهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r6.claim: The consequence clause answers the negation, while the next clause answers the prohibition; alternatively, being unjust is caused by dismissing them.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p324#3/r6.anchor: جواب النفى وهو ما عليك من حسابهم

ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r1.claim: Polytheists tried to make the Prophet dismiss poor followers so the elite would sit with him; they meant Suhayb, Khabbāb, ʿAmmār, Salmān, and Bilāl.
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r1.anchor: فقالوا لو باعدت عنك هؤلاء السفلة والعبيد لجلس إليك الكبراء والأشراف

ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r2.claim: God prioritized religion, forbade dismissing those sincere in seeking Him and following His commands, and exposed the leaders’ attempt to use their exclusion as an argument against the Prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r2.anchor: فأعلم الله عز وجل، أن أمر الدين هو المقدم

ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r3.claim: The story of Noah shows that messengers were also followed by people whom their elites called low-status.
ZAJJAJ:v2p251#2/r3.anchor: في قصة نوح إنه اتبع نوحا من كان عندهم من أراذلهم

ZAJJAJ:v2p252/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p252/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p252/r1.claim: ‘Then you would be among wrongdoers’ answers the prohibition against driving them away; ‘then you would drive them away’ follows from the statement that neither side is accountable for the other.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r1.speaker: المشركون
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r1.claim: The polytheists objected to sitting with poor believers such as Salman, Suhayb, Bilal, and Khabbab, and asked that they be dismissed; the Prophet considered it but did not expel them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r1.anchor: ولا نرضى بمجالسة أمثال هؤلاء يعنون سلمان وصهيبا وبلالا وخبابا فاطردهم عنك

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r2.claim: The Prophet inclined toward their request only in hope of converting them and their people, thinking it would neither harm nor diminish the poor companions; revelation forbade the contemplated expulsion.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r2.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما مال إلى ذلك طمعا في إسلامهم، وإسلام قومهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r3.claim: In Muslim’s report, Sa‘d and five other companions were present when the polytheists asked the Prophet to dismiss them, and revelation came after he reflected on the request.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r3.anchor: روى مسلم عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة نفر،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Hasan interpret morning and evening invocation as keeping the obligatory prayers in congregation.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r5.claim: Other explanations take the invocation as remembrance and Qur’an recitation, or as prayers at daybreak and evening for guidance and forgiveness.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r5.anchor: وقيل: الذكر وقراءة القرآن. ويحتمل أن يريد الدعاء في أول النهار وآخره

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r6.claim: ‘Seeking His face’ can mean sincerely seeking God’s obedience, or seeking God Himself, who is described as possessing the Face.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r6.anchor: أي طاعته، والإخلاص فيها، أي يخلصون في عبادتهم وأعمالهم لله،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r7.claim: Morning and evening are specified because people are usually occupied then, so one devoted to worship during busy hours is still more devoted in free time.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r7.anchor: وخص الغداة والعشي بالذكر لأن الشغل غالب فيهما على الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r8.claim: The Prophet later obeyed the command in 18:28 to remain with these worshippers, not looking away to seek worldly display.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52/r8.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك يصبر نفسه معهم كما أمره الله في قوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r1.speaker: خباب
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r1.claim: Khabbab’s Ibn Majah report says al-Aqra‘ and ‘Uyayna sought a private session because Arab delegations might see them with poor believers; the Prophet agreed before revelation forbade dismissing them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r1.anchor: عن خباب في قول الله عز وجل: { ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي }

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r2.claim: After revelation, the Prophet sat with the poor companions and did not rise until they chose to leave.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#2/r2.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس معنا فإذا أراد أن يقوم قام وتركنا

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r1.speaker: سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r1.claim: Sa‘d reports that Quraysh rejected following six poor companions, including Sa‘d, Ibn Mas‘ud, Suhayb, ‘Ammar, al-Miqdad, and Bilal; revelation answered their demand.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r1.anchor: عن سعد قال: نزلت هذه الآية فينا ستة، في وفي ابن مسعود وصهيب وعمار والمقداد وبلال

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r2.claim: ‘You are not responsible for their account’ means their judgment and provision belong to God, as do the Prophet’s; the first min is partitive and the second emphatic extra.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r3.claim: Since God alone provides and judges, the Prophet must receive and sit with them; expelling them to accommodate people of lesser faith would be injustice.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r3.anchor: فأقبل عليهم وجالسهم ولا تطردهم مراعاة لحق من ليس على مثل حالهم

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r4.claim: The warning is instruction for others, not evidence that the Prophet actually expelled anyone; it resembles the conditional warning against shirk though he would never commit it.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r4.anchor: وحاشاه من وقوع ذلك منه، وإنما هذا بيان للأحكام،

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r5.claim: The syntax makes ‘then you would expel them’ a result of the preceding negation and ‘so you would be unjust’ a result of the prohibition; the clauses can also be reordered.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r6.claim: The verse and report forbid elevating people for status or fine clothing and despising those who are obscure or poorly dressed.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:52#3/r6.anchor: وقد حصل من قوة الآية والحديث النهي عن أن يعظم أحد لجاهه ولثوبه،

RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r1.speaker: عبدالله بن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Quraysh leaders asked Muhammad to dismiss poor believers such as Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, and Ammar so they might follow him; he refused, then agreed to separate meeting times in hope they would convert.
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r1.anchor: روي عن عبدالله بن مسعود أنه قال : مر الملأ من قريش على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r2.claim: After the leaders demanded a written agreement and Umar suggested trying their request, this verse descended; the Prophet threw away the page, Umar apologized, and Salman and Khabbab said it concerned them.
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r2.anchor: فنزلت هذه الآية ، فرمى الصحيفة ، واعتذر عمر عن مقالته

RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r3.speaker: سلمان وخباب
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r3.claim: Salman and Khabbab say the Prophet then sat with them until his knees touched theirs; after 18:28 he stopped rising before them and praised God for being commanded to stay with them in life and death.
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r3.anchor: فنزل قوله { واصبر نفسك مع الذين يدعون ربهم } ( الكهف : 28 ) فترك القيام عنا إلى أن نقوم عنه

RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r4.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r4.claim: Critics cite the incident as sin: the Prophet expelled poor believers despite the prohibition, became one of the wrongdoers, contradicted Noah's refusal to expel believers and the command to follow prophets, sought worldly adornment, and later said God rebuked him.
RAZI-FULL:v12p193/r4.anchor: احتج الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء عليهم السلام بهذه الآية من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r1.claim: Razi says Muhammad did not dismiss them from contempt for poverty; he set separate meeting times to win Quraysh, whose conversion mattered greatly, and any mistaken judgment in this effort is forgiven.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r1.anchor: ما طردهم لأجل الاستخفاف بهم والاستنكاف من فقرهم وإنما عين لجلوسهم وقتا معينا

RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r2.claim: Calling their dismissal wrongful means the poor deserved honor; expelling them from that gathering wronged them by leaving the more fitting and excellent course, not by violating a duty. The other criticisms likewise concern what was preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r2.anchor: كان ذلك ظلما ، إلا أنه من باب ترك الأولى والأفضل لا من باب ترك الواجبات

RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r3.claim: Ibn Amir reads بالغدوة with waw and a damma on ghayn, also in 18:28; the other readers have the common form بالغداة with alif and a fatha.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر { بالغداة والعشى } بالواو وضم الغين وفي سورة الكهف مثله

RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r4.claim: Al-Farisi favors the common reading because ghadāh is an indefinite noun that can take the definite article, while ghudwah is a proper name; spelling ṣalāh with waw despite its alif sound shows orthography proves nothing.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r4.anchor: الوجه قراءة العامة بالغدة لأنها تستعمل نكرة فأمكن تعريفها بإدخال لام التعريف عليها

RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r5.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r5.claim: Sibawayh says ghudwah and bukrah can function as generic names like Umm Hubayn; Yunus reports Abu Amr leaves them uninflected when used definitely, supporting the common reading, while al-Khalil permits them like ḍuḥwah, supporting Ibn Amir.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194/r5.anchor: زعم الخليل أنه يجوز أن يقال أتيتك اليوم غدوة وبكرة فجعلهما بمنزلة ضحوة

RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Hasan, and Mujahid take calling upon God at dawn and evening to mean the prescribed dawn and afternoon prayers; another explanation treats the two ends of the day as shorthand for keeping all five prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r1.anchor: أن المراد من الدعاء الصلاة ، يعني يعبدون ربهم بالصلاة المكتوبة

RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r2.claim: Ibrahim takes الدعاء to mean remembrance: the poor believers remember God at the two ends of the day.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r2.anchor: قال إبراهيم : الدعاء ههنا هو الذكر والمعنى يذكرون ربهم طرفي النهار

RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r3.speaker: المجسمة
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r3.claim: The anthropomorphists cite wanting God's face and related verses such as 55:27 as evidence that God has bodily parts; Razi answers that God's complete oneness in 112:1 rules out composition.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r3.anchor: المجسمة تمسكوا في إثبات الأعضاء لله تعالى بقوله { يريدون وجهه }

RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r4.claim: Face is either an honorific way to refer to God Himself, like face of an argument, or a metonym for love and seeking approval because a lover wants to see the beloved's face; compare 2:115.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r4.anchor: جعل الوجه كناية عن المحبة وطلب الرضا

RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r5.claim: One reading makes the pronouns in the account clause refer to the disbelievers: the Prophet need not bear their account or worry whether the proposed meeting leads them to Islam, since God guides and governs them.
RAZI-FULL:v12p194#2/r5.anchor: والقول الأول : أنه عائد إلى المشركين ، والمعنى ما عليك من حساب المشركين من شيء

RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r1.claim: The more apparent reading refers the account pronouns to the poor worshippers, since the pronoun in the warning about expelling them certainly refers to those believers and the nearby pronouns should match.
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r1.anchor: القول الثاني : أن الضمير عائد إلى الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي ، وهم الفقراء

RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r2.claim: The disbelievers accused the poor of joining for food and clothes rather than faith; if so, Muhammad need only judge appearances, while their hidden account belongs to them, as no bearer carries another's burden.
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r2.anchor: إن الكفار طعنوا في إيمان أولئك الفقراء وقالوا يا محمد إنهم إنما اجتمعوا عندك

RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r3.claim: Both clauses are needed to express one reciprocal point: neither Muhammad nor the poor will be held responsible for the other's account.
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r3.anchor: جعلت الجملتان بمنزلة جملة واحدة قصد بهما معنى واحد

RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r4.claim: A second interpretation is that Muhammad bears no responsibility for their livelihood and they bear none for his; God provides for both, so he should let them remain rather than expel them.
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r4.anchor: ما عليك من حساب رزقهم من شيء فتملهم وتطردهم

RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r5.claim: The episode resembles Noah's exchange with his people over his low-status followers: 26:111-113 describes laborers and craftsmen, and their account belongs to God. The expulsion clause answers the denial; being unjust may mean wronging himself or the poor who deserved welcome.
RAZI-FULL:v12p195/r5.anchor: وقوله { فتطردهم } جواب النفي ومعناه ، ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء فتطردهم

ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r1.claim: Traditions place the revelation of this and the next verse after Meccan pagan leaders offered to consider Islam if Muhammad dismissed former slaves and other low-status followers; he rejected their demand.
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r1.anchor: some of the pagan chieftains at Mecca expressed their willingness to consider accepting Islam on the condition

ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r2.claim: Asad says the historical occasion is not a full explanation: the verse's wording concerns people who believe in God and seek His grace, even if they are not Muslims in the current sense.
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r2.anchor: while not being Muslims in the current sense of this word

ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r3.claim: The enduring instruction applies to all Qur'an followers: do not repel anyone who believes in God, even with incomplete Qur'anic beliefs; instead explain the teaching patiently.
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n41/r3.anchor: they are enjoined not to repulse anyone who believes in God - even though his beliefs may not fully answer

ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n42/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n42/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n42/r1.claim: The reciprocal accountability clause means people answer to God alone for beliefs or conduct that differ from Qur'anic teaching.
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n42/r1.anchor: all are accountable to God alone

ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n43/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n43/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n43/r1.claim: The literal phrase means that repelling them would make the addressee one of the evildoers.
ASAD-NOTES:6:52#n43/r1.anchor: so that thou shouldst repulse them and thus be of the evildoers

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r1.claim: Prominent Makkans wanted to join the Prophet’s teaching circle but disliked association with lower-status followers and asked him to send them away.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r1.anchor: This verse was reportedly revealed when a group of prominent Makkans indicated that they wished to join the Prophet’s teaching circle

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r2.claim: Some reports say the Makkans asked only that the poor followers be moved to the back rows of prayer, not expelled altogether.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r2.anchor: Some reports indicate the Prophet was not asked to send away these followers altogether, but rather to send them to the back rows of prayer

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r3.claim: The Prophet refused to drive away his poorer followers, as Noah refused similar demands, though he was prepared to have them depart temporarily when prominent Makkans visited.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r3.anchor: The Prophet refused to “drive away” his poorer followers (in 11:27–29 and 26:111–14 Noah refuses to do the same)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r4.speaker: IK, R, Ṭ, W
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r4.claim: The verse was revealed to forbid the Prophet from driving away his pious followers who worship morning and evening.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r4.anchor: This verse was then revealed forbidding him from “driving away” his pious followers who call upon their Lord morning and evening (IK, R, Ṭ, W)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r5.speaker: Ṭ, W
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r5.claim: Quran 18:28 is linked to a similar circumstance and is reportedly a revelation about that situation.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r5.anchor: reportedly revealed in a similar circumstance (Ṭ, W)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r6.claim: Quran 80:1–10 recounts the incident in which the Prophet is admonished for showing displeasure when a poor blind man came instead of wealthier Makkans.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r6.anchor: about the incident in which the Prophet is admonished for registering displeasure when his teaching attracted a poor blind man rather than the wealthier Makkans

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r7.claim: These passages raise the question of how the Prophet could appear to favor status-conscious Makkans over sincere followers, given that driving them away would make him a wrongdoer.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r7.anchor: These passages raise the question of how the Prophet could seem to favor these prominent Makkans

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r8.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī says the Prophet’s possible initial willingness to accommodate the Makkans was intended only to facilitate their acceptance of Islam.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r8.anchor: al-Rāzī argues that even if the Prophet were initially prepared to accede to the Makkans’ demand

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r9.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī reasons that the poor followers could be instructed another time, so no spiritual harm would come to them.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r9.anchor: his intention was only to facilitate their acceptance of Islam, and since the Prophet could continue to instruct his poorer followers at another time

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r10.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī holds that the Prophet did not sin by initially appearing willing to accommodate the demand because his intention was good.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r10.anchor: cannot be said to have sinned in his apparent initial willingness to accommodate the Makkans’ demand (R)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r11.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r11.claim: Morning and evening invocation may mean the five canonical prayers performed at their appointed times.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r11.anchor: refer to praying the five canonical prayers at their prescribed times

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r12.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r12.claim: Morning and evening invocation may mean supererogatory remembrance of God or Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r12.anchor: performing supererogatory acts of invoking God

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r13.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r13.claim: The invocation may include all these practices together.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r13.anchor: or to all of them (R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r14.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r14.claim: Desiring God’s Face can mean literally hoping to see it, as a sincere lover longs to see the beloved’s face.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r14.anchor: with the hope of seeing God’s Face, for any sincere lover longs to see the face of the beloved (R)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r15.speaker: IK, R
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r15.claim: Desiring God’s Face can also metaphorically mean sincerity of intention among the Prophet’s followers.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r15.anchor: it refers metaphorically to sincerity of intention among the Prophet’s followers (IK, R)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r16.claim: The verse echoes the Quranic principle that no person bears another’s burden.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r16.anchor: echoes the Quranic idea that none shall bear the burden of another (6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r17.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r17.claim: Syntactically, “their reckoning” most likely refers to the pious worshippers’ own reckoning, so the Prophet judges piety by outward acts.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r17.anchor: that the Prophet need only judge his followers’ piety on the basis of their outward actions (Z)

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r18.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r18.claim: Some commentators say the verse responds to a Quraysh accusation that the poor followed the Prophet for material support rather than religious sincerity.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r18.anchor: Some commentators explain this as a response to an accusation made by some of the Quraysh

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r19.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r19.claim: On that reading, the Prophet need not assess possible ulterior motives behind his followers’ apparent piety.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r19.anchor: the verse was meant to indicate that the Prophet had no responsibility to assess the possible ulterior motives behind his

STUDYQURAN:6:52/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r20.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r20.claim: More plausibly, the reckoning concerns the prominent Makkans; the Prophet need not court their conversion by yielding to their demand to dismiss sincere followers.
STUDYQURAN:6:52/r20.anchor: their embracing Islam that he should accede to their demand and “drive away”his pious followers at their behest (Z)

TAB-FULL:v9p258/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Quraysh leaders saw Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, Khabbab, and other poor Muslims with the Prophet and demanded their dismissal, promising to follow if he did so.
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، قال: " مر الملأ من قريش بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v9p258/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also reports that Quraysh leaders passed by the Prophet and made the same request to exclude his poor companions.
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: مر على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ملأ من قريش، ثم ذكر نحوه

TAB-FULL:v9p258/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r3.speaker: خباب
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r3.claim: Khabbab reports that al-Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn asked for a separate audience, embarrassed to be seen with poor believers; after the revelation the Prophet called the believers back and greeted them, then stayed with them.
TAB-FULL:v9p258/r3.anchor: عن أبي الكنود، عن خباب، في قول الله تعالى

TAB-FULL:v9p261/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r1.claim: Khabbab’s account repeats that the two elite men shunned the poor companions; after the revelation the Prophet called them near and sat with them until he rose.
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r1.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت، بنحو حديث الحسين بن عمرو، إلا أنه قال في حديثه: فلما رأوهم حوله نفروهم

TAB-FULL:v9p261/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r2.claim: Qatada says Quraysh unbelievers offered to follow Muhammad if he expelled named poor Muslims whom they looked down on.
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

TAB-FULL:v9p261/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r3.speaker: الكلبي
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi is also cited for the report that Quraysh demanded the expulsion of poor Muslims as a condition of following Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r3.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، والكلبي، أن ناسا، من كفار قريش قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v9p261/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the companions as Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd, whom Quraysh belittled and said they would not sit with.
TAB-FULL:v9p261/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

TAB-FULL:v9p262/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p262/r1.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v9p262/r1.claim: Sa'id says six Companions, including Ibn Masud, used to arrive early, sit near the Prophet, and listen; Quraysh objected that these men were being given precedence.

TAB-FULL:v9p262/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p262/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v9p262/r2.claim: Ikrima says prominent Quraysh approached Abu Talib, offering to follow Muhammad if he expelled their clients and allies; Umar suggested trying their request, and the verse was revealed about the poor believers, including named freedmen and allies.
TAB-FULL:v9p262/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عكرمة، في قوله

TAB-FULL:v9p263/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that a man was ashamed to be seen with Salman and Bilal and asked Muhammad to dismiss them; the revelation warns that expelling them would make him unjust and commands that they be greeted and reassured of mercy.
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد: قال رجل للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إني أستحيي من الله أن يراني مع سلمان وبلال وذويهم

TAB-FULL:v9p263/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “calling on their Lord morning and evening” as worship through the obligatory prayers.
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، قوله

TAB-FULL:v9p263/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r3.claim: Ibrahim identifies the phrase with the five obligatory prayers and argues against interpreting it as attendance at preachers’ gatherings.
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r3.anchor: عن أبي حمزة، عن إبراهيم، في قوله

TAB-FULL:v9p263/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v9p263/r4.claim: Ibrahim also glosses the phrase simply as prayer.

TAB-FULL:v9p265/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r1.claim: Mujahid says the phrase means the obligatory dawn and afternoon prayers.
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

TAB-FULL:v9p265/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r3.claim: Mujahid again identifies them as those who perform the obligatory prayer.
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله

TAB-FULL:v9p265/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v9p265/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says they worship God morning and evening by performing the obligatory prayer.

TAB-FULL:v9p266/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r1.claim: Mujahid says the callers are the praying believers Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd.

TAB-FULL:v9p266/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r2.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib rejects using the verse to defend post-prayer storytelling: it refers to the prayer the group had just finished.
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r2.anchor: فقال سعيد: " ما أسرعهم إلى هذا المجلس

TAB-FULL:v9p266/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن أبي عمرة
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r3.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Umra identifies the callers with the obligatory prayer.
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عمرة، قال: «الصلاة المكتوبة»

TAB-FULL:v9p266/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r4.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r4.claim: Amir likewise says the verse refers to prayer.
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r4.anchor: عن إسرائيل، عن جابر، عن عامر، قال: «هي الصلاة»

TAB-FULL:v9p266/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r5.claim: Qatada specifies the dawn and afternoon prayers.
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه}

TAB-FULL:v9p266/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r6.claim: Mujahid recounts that Abd al-Rahman redirected a crowd seeking storytelling to the prayer that had just ended, saying the verse concerns prayer.
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: صلى عبد الرحمن في مسجد الرسول، فلما صلى قام فاستند إلى حجرة النبي

TAB-FULL:v9p266/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r7.claim: Another view says elites asked only that poor believers be moved behind them in the prayer rows, not expelled from the Prophet’s gathering altogether.
TAB-FULL:v9p266/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي الصلاة، ولكن القوم لم يسألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم طرد هؤلاء الضعفاء عن مجلسه

TAB-FULL:v9p267/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says some poor companions were with the Prophet when nobles offered to believe if the poor prayed behind them.
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وكذلك فتنا بعضهم ببعض}

TAB-FULL:v9p267/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r2.claim: Ibrahim identifies the callers as people engaged in remembrance of God.
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r2.anchor: عن سفيان، عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، قوله: {ولا تطرد

TAB-FULL:v9p267/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r3.claim: Ibrahim also explains the command as not excluding them from remembrance.
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r3.anchor: عن منصور: {ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

TAB-FULL:v9p267/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak takes “calling on their Lord” to mean worship, citing 40:43 where what people call upon means what they worship.
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي}

TAB-FULL:v9p267/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r6.claim: Al-Tabari says الدعاء may include spoken remembrance, glorification, praise, required and voluntary acts; since God calls worship دعاء, the group may have combined all these, and no narrower interpretation is demonstrably superior.
TAB-FULL:v9p267/r6.anchor: والدعاء لله يكون بذكره وتمجيده والثناء عليه قولا وكلاما، وقد يكون بالعمل له بالجوارح الأعمال

TAB-FULL:v9p270/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r1.claim: The companions sought pardon and forgiveness through righteous deeds, obligatory duties, voluntary worship, and remembrance of God morning and evening, seeking nearness to Him.
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r1.anchor: يسألون عفوه ومغفرته لصالح أعمالهم وأداء ما ألزمهم من فرائضه ونوافل تطوعهم وذكرهم إياه بألسنتهم

TAB-FULL:v9p270/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r2.claim: The mutual-accountability clause means the Prophet is not accountable for their provision, nor they for his; fear of being judged over worldly provision must not prompt their expulsion.
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r2.anchor: ما عليك من حساب ما رزقتهم من الرزق من شيء، وما عليهم من حساب ما رزقتك من الرزق من شيء

TAB-FULL:v9p270/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p270/r3.claim: Grammatically, فتطردهم answers the preceding statement that neither party is accountable for the other, while فتكون answers the prohibition against expelling them.

TABATABAI:6:51-52/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:51-52/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:51-52/r4.claim: Some commentators say the people singled out are believers who affirm resurrection and are the poor believers mentioned in the next verse.
TABATABAI:6:51-52/r4.anchor: في المؤمنين القائلين بالحشر، وأنهم هم الذين عنوا في الآية التالية

TABATABAI:6:52-53/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:52-53/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:52-53/r3.claim: The context indicates that Meccan polytheists asked the Prophet to expel poor believers; this resembles elites in Noah's community demanding the same of him.
TABATABAI:6:52-53/r3.anchor: أن المشركين من قومه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم اقترحوا عليه أن يطرد عن نفسه الضعفاء المؤمنين به

TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r1.claim: God has no bodily face or material direction; “face” is what something faces others with, so it can metaphorically denote the direction or aspect by which it is encountered.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r1.anchor: لكن وجه الشيء لما كان ما يستقبل به غيره كانت الجهة بمعنى الناحية

TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r2.claim: Righteous works can be a face oriented toward God, while evil works face Satan; divine attributes and names are also ways creation encounters God.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r2.anchor: وبهذه العناية تصير الأعمال الصالحة وجها لله تعالى كما أن الأعمال الطالحة وجه للشيطان

TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r3.claim: The phrase “possessor of majesty and honor” grammatically describes the face, not the Lord, in the verse about God's enduring face.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r3.anchor: فإن ظاهر الآية أن قوله { ذو الجلال والإكرام } نعت للوجه دون الرب

TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r4.claim: Anything related to divine nearness—God's names, attributes, religion, good deeds, prophets, angels, martyrs, and forgiven believers—is a face of God.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r4.anchor: وكذا كل من يحل في ساحة قربه كالأنبياء والملائكة والشهداء وكل مغفور له من المؤمنين وجه له تعالى

TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r5.claim: These near-to-God realities endure by God's permanence; “everything perishes except His face” identifies them as remaining in His secure presence.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#6/r5.anchor: فدل الحصر الذي في الآية على أن ذلك كله وجه لله سبحانه

TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r1.claim: What worshippers seek from God is His face, including divine favor, mercy, satisfaction, and the means of nearness to Him.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r1.anchor: فكل ذلك وجهه تعالى لأن صفات فعله تعالى كالرحمة والمرضاة والفضل ونحو ذلك من وجهه

TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r2.claim: “Account” originally denotes numerical reckoning and extends to measuring deeds for recompense; because reward is God's, the reckoning is His responsibility.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#7/r2.anchor: فالحساب على الله تعالى أي في عهدته وكفايته

TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r1.claim: A report calls those who deny divine decree and claim independent human will and power the Magians of this community.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r1.anchor: قال فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم " ألا إن لكل أمه مجوسا

TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i explains the hadith as condemning those who deny God's relation to human acts and make humans independent creators, like Zoroastrian dualism.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r2.anchor: وهو أن لإرادة الله سبحانه تعلقا ما بأعمال العباد

TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r3.claim: The Mu'tazilites reinterpret the hadith to target those who affirm decree, claiming they resemble Magians by assigning good and evil to a creator other than humans.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r3.anchor: وقد أول المعتزلة وهم النافون للقدر الرواية بأن المراد بالقدرية المثبتون للقدر

TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r4.claim: The manuscript readings that combine “no decree” with denial of human will contradict each other, so al-Tabataba'i attributes that combination to scribal corruption.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#8/r4.anchor: والقول بالقدر يلازم القول بنفي استقلاله بالمشيئة والقدرة

TABATABAI:6:37-55#9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#9/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABATABAI:6:37-55#9/r8.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reports that Quraysh leaders asked the Prophet to expel poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Ammar, Bilal, and Khabbab so they might follow him.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#9/r8.anchor: مر الملأ من قريش على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وعنده صهيب وعمار وبلال وخباب

TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r1.claim: Ikrimah's report says Quraysh nobles asked Abu Talib to have the Prophet remove enslaved and poor followers; Umar suggested complying, then verses about warning and grateful believers were revealed.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r1.anchor: فذكر ذلك أبو طالب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فقال عمر لو فعلت يا رسول الله

TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r2.speaker: خباب
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r2.claim: Khabbab reports that al-Aqra' and Uyayna demanded an exclusive audience away from poor believers; Gabriel delivered the prohibition, and the Prophet thereafter stayed seated with them until he chose to rise.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r2.anchor: جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينة بن حصين الفزاري فوجدا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قاعدا مع بلال وصهيب وعمار وخباب

TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i treats these similar stories as applications of the verses, not separate revelation occasions: the sura came down all at once, and the same proposal may have recurred.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#10/r3.anchor: إنما هي من قبيل ما نسميه تطبيقا بمعنى أنهم وجدوا مضامين بعض الآيات تقبل الانطباق على بعض القصص الواقعة

TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r1.claim: Reports giving occasions of revelation for this Meccan surah often relate events merely associated with the verses; paraphrase, weak transmission, and fabrication prevent treating them as exclusive causes.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r1.anchor: فلا اعتماد في أمثال هذه السورة من السور التي نزلت دفعة

TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r2.speaker: عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r2.claim: A report says the verse came after some people proposed that the Prophet expel the poor Companions of the Suffa.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r2.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد الله بن المهاجر أن الآية نزلت في اقتراح بعض الناس

TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r3.claim: He rejects that as a specific occasion because the surah was revealed all at once in Mecca, before the Hijra.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r3.anchor: ويضعفه ما تقدم في نظيره أن السورة إنما نزلت دفعة وفي مكة قبل الهجرة

TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r6.claim: Reports assigning preceding verses to enemies of the Prophet’s family are applications or inner interpretations, not occasions of revelation, given the surah’s Meccan, single-period descent.
TABATABAI:6:37-55#11/r6.anchor: والظاهر أنها جميعا من قبيل الجري والتطبيق أو الأخذ بباطن المعنى

TABRISI:6:52-53/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
TABRISI:6:52-53/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the temporal phrase with wāw as al-ghudwa throughout the Qurʾan; the other readers read al-ghadāh with alif.
TABRISI:6:52-53/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر بالغدوة والعشي في كل القرآن بواو والباقون بالغداة بالألف

TABRISI:6:52-53/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:6:52-53/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī argues al-ghadāh is preferable because it is an indefinite noun that can take the article, whereas ghudwa is a proper name and does not become indefinite; the grammarians' reports also support ghudāh.
TABRISI:6:52-53/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: الوجه الغداة لأنها تستعمل نكرة

TABRISI:6:52-53/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53/r3.speaker: الخليل
TABRISI:6:52-53/r3.claim: The reading ghudwa is also defended: al-Khalīl allows it as a temporal adverb like ḍuḥwa, and other time names can appear definite without the article.
TABRISI:6:52-53/r3.anchor: ووجه قراءة ابن عامر أن سيبويه قال زعم الخليل أنه يجوز أن تقول

TABRISI:6:52-53/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53/r4.claim: “Then you would expel them” answers the preceding negation, and “then you would be among the wrongdoers” is subjunctive as the result of the prohibition not to expel.
TABRISI:6:52-53/r4.anchor: فتطردهم جواب للنفي في قوله ما عليك من حسابهم

TABRISI:6:52-53/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:6:52-53/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports Quraysh leaders passing the Prophet while he sat with poor Muslims—Ṣuhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl, and ʿAmmār—and asking him to expel them so the leaders might follow him.
TABRISI:6:52-53/r5.anchor: روى الثعلبي بإسناده عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال مر الملأ من قريش على رسول الله

TABRISI:6:52-53/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53/r6.speaker: سلمان
TABRISI:6:52-53/r6.claim: Salmān and Khabbāb say the verse was revealed concerning them.
TABRISI:6:52-53/r6.anchor: وقال سلمان وخباب: فينا نزلت هذه الآية

TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r1.claim: A report describes al-Aqraʿ b. Ḥābis, ʿUyayna b. Ḥiṣn, and other leaders disparaging the poor believers and asking the Prophet to dismiss them when Arab delegations came; he agrees, but Gabriel reveals the prohibition and the Prophet tears up their proposed written pledge.
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r1.anchor: جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينه بن حصين الفزاري وذووهم من المؤلفة قلوبهم

TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r2.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r2.claim: After the revelation, the Prophet tells the believers that their Lord has prescribed mercy, then quotes God's instruction to keep patient company with them and says he will live and die among them.
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r2.anchor: فكنا نقعد معه فإذا أراد أن يقوم

TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r3.claim: God forbids His Messenger from acceding to the polytheists' demand to expel the believers who worship Him at dawn and evening.
TABRISI:6:52-53#2/r3.anchor: ثم نهى سبحانه رسوله عليه واله السلام عن إجابة المشركين

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r1.claim: The cited words from Noah say that their reckoning rests with the Lord alone, supporting the interpretation that God alone will judge the believers deeds.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r1.anchor: إن حسابهم إلا على ربي لو تشعرون

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r2.claim: The polytheists despised the poor believers because of their poverty and devotion, wanting them set below themselves in the gathering; the verse rebuts this social contempt.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r2.anchor: وهذا لأن المشركين أزدروهم لفقرهم وحاجتهم إلى الأعمال الدينية

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r3.claim: A second interpretation says the Prophet is not responsible for believers livelihood, so poverty is no reason to tire of them and expel them.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r3.anchor: ما عليك من حساب رزقهم من شيء فتملهم وتطردهم

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r4.claim: God provides both the poor believers and the Prophet, so neither party depends on the other for provision.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r4.anchor: أي ليس رزقهم عليك ولا رزقك عليهم وإنما يرزقك وإياهم الله

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the warning as saying the Prophet would wrong the believers if he expelled them; Ibn ʿAbbās says such expulsion would harm the Prophet himself through disobedience.

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the warning is severe because the Prophet had considered preferring wealthy leaders to attract their followers, intending good rather than contempt for the poor, but God forbade it.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r6.anchor: عظم الأمر في هذا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وخوف الدخول في جملة الظالمين

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r7.claim: God tests wealthy leaders through poor believers: a proud notable may refuse faith when a poorer person has preceded him, lest he lose precedence.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r7.anchor: ابتلينا هؤلاء الرؤساء من قريش بالموالي فإذا نظر الشريف إلى الوضيع قد آمن قبله

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r8.claim: God is described as testing though He needs no test because He treats people as a tester would; the outcome clause means the affair resulted in their asking whether God favored these believers.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r8.anchor: وهو لا يحتاج إلى الاختبار لأنه عاملهم معاملة المختبر

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r9.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r9.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī interprets the test as the difficult obligation imposed on Arab nobles to believe and give precedence to those who believed first; the clause lets believers accept the Prophet's honor toward them rather than denying God's favor.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r9.anchor: المعنى في فتنا شددنا التكليف على إشراف العرب بأن أمرناهم بالإيمان

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r10.claim: The lām in the outcome clause marks consequence: God acted so they might be patient and grateful, and their question was the eventual outcome.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r10.anchor: هذه لام العاقبة المعنى فعلنا هذا ليصبروا ويشكروا

TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r11.claim: The question whether God knows the grateful is a confirming question, as illustrated by Jarīr poetry.
TABRISI:6:52-53#3/r11.anchor: هذا استفهام تقرير أي إنه كذلك كقول جرير

THALABI:v4p149/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p149/r3.speaker: سليمان وخباب بن الأرت
THALABI:v4p149/r3.claim: Suleiman and Khabbab say the command not to dismiss the worshippers was revealed about them.
THALABI:v4p149/r3.anchor: خباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت هذه الآية

THALABI:v4p149/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p149/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p149/r4.claim: Al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna looked down on the poorly dressed believers and asked the Prophet to seat them elsewhere; he refused to expel believers.

THALABI:v4p149/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p149/r5.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v4p149/r5.claim: The Prophet refused the request to remove the believers, and Gabriel interrupted the attempt to write an agreement by revealing the prohibition.

THALABI:v4p149/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p149/r6.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v4p149/r6.claim: The Prophet stayed with the poor believers, sitting close and waiting for them rather than leaving them behind.
THALABI:v4p149/r6.anchor: الحمد لله الذي لم يمتني حتى أمرني أن أصبر نفسي مع قوم من أمتي

THALABI:v4p150/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150/r1.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p150/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says the chiefs proposed separate days or one shared assembly where the Prophet would face them and turn his back to the poor; God forbade it.
THALABI:v4p150/r1.anchor: قالوا له: اجعل لنا يوما ولهم يوم، قال: لا أفعل

THALABI:v4p150/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v4p150/r2.claim: Quraysh scorned the poor followers and promised to follow Muhammad if he expelled them; they specifically named Bilal and Ibn Umm ʿAbd.
THALABI:v4p150/r2.anchor: أرضيت بهؤلاء من قومك؟ أفنحن نكون تبعا لهؤلاء

THALABI:v4p150/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v4p150/r3.claim: After leading Quraysh appealed through Abu Talib to expel poor adherents, Umar suggested testing what the chiefs wanted; the verse followed and Umar apologized.
THALABI:v4p150/r3.anchor: لو فعلت ذلك حتى ننظر ما الذي يريدون وإلى ما يصيرون فنزلت من قولهم هذه الآية

THALABI:v4p150/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150/r4.speaker: جبير بن نفيل
THALABI:v4p150/r4.claim: Quraysh called the poor believers riffraff and asked that they be removed so Quraysh could become the Prophet’s companions.
THALABI:v4p150/r4.anchor: أرسلت إلينا فاطرد هؤلاء السقاط عنك فنكون أصحابك

THALABI:v4p150/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p150/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the worshippers are poor people who prayed the obligatory dawn and afternoon prayers; nobles sought to displace them in the prayer line.
THALABI:v4p150/r5.anchor: يدعون ربهم يعني يعبدون ربهم بالصلاة المكتوبة بالغداة والعشي

THALABI:v4p150#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
