THALABI:v4p150#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan explains that the believers to be kept close are those who preserve congregational prayer.
THALABI:v4p150#2/r1.anchor: لا ولكنهم المحافظون على الصلوات في الجماعة

THALABI:v4p150#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v4p150#2/r2.claim: Saʿid tells Mujahid that the verse refers to people at prayer, not those rushing to a storyteller after morning prayer.
THALABI:v4p150#2/r2.anchor: إنما ذلك في الصلاة التي انصرفا عنها الآن

THALABI:v4p150#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p150#2/r3.claim: Mujahid takes the verse to support attending a remembrance gathering after the dawn prayer.
THALABI:v4p150#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: صليت الصبح مع سعيد بن المسيب

THALABI:v4p150#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150#2/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v4p150#2/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says they recite the Qurʾan seeking God’s countenance; the clause about accountability answers the objection, and the prohibition clause governs the consequence.
THALABI:v4p150#2/r4.anchor: يعني يقرءون القرآن يريدون وجهه جواب لقوله ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء

THALABI:v4p150#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v4p150#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says some nobles refused Islam after seeing a low-status person accept it first, out of pride at being preceded.
THALABI:v4p150#2/r5.anchor: كان الشريف إذا نظر إلى الوضيع قد آمن قبله حمى أنفا أن يسلم

THALABI:v4p150#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p150#2/r6.claim: The question ‘Has God favored these among us?’ is answered by saying God knows best who is grateful for Islam and deserves guidance.
THALABI:v4p150#2/r6.anchor: أليس الله بأعلم بالشاكرين يعني المؤمنين

THALABI:v4p150#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p150#2/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v4p150#2/r7.claim: The Prophet sat among destitute migrants listening to Qurʾan and promised that the poor would enter Paradise half a day—five hundred years—before wealthy believers.
THALABI:v4p150#2/r7.anchor: تدخلون الجنة قبل أغنياء المؤمنين بنصف يوم مقداره خمس مائة سنة

THALABI:v4p151/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p151/r1.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v4p151/r1.claim: The Prophet says God approved his example of sitting with poor believers and calls their assembly a gathering of earlier prophets and righteous people.
THALABI:v4p151/r1.anchor: إن الله رضي لي أن أتأسى بمجالسكم وأن الله معنا

THALABI:v4p151/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p151/r2.speaker: عائذ بن عمرو
THALABI:v4p151/r2.claim: After Abu Bakr rebuked Salman, Suhayb, and Bilal for insulting Abu Sufyan, the Prophet warned that upsetting them upsets God; they forgave Abu Bakr.
THALABI:v4p151/r2.anchor: لعلك أغضبتهم إن كنت أغضبتهم فقد أغضبت ربك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Quraysh leaders asked Muhammad to expel Suhayb, Khabbab, Bilal, Ammar, and other poor Muslims, promising to follow him if he did.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: (مر الملأ من قريش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r2.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r2.claim: Khabbab says Uyayna ibn Hisn and al-Aqra ibn Habis asked the Prophet to remove poor enslaved believers while Arab delegations visited, so they would not be seen with them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r2.anchor: لا يحسن بنا الجلوس مع هؤلاء العبيد الفقراء، فأقمهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r3.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r3.claim: In Khabbab's account, the Prophet agreed and summoned Ali to write their demand, but revelation came; he set aside the page, turned to the poor Muslims, and drew near to them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r3.anchor: فأنزلت هذه الآية وما بعدها، فنحى رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the Prophet considered prioritizing wealthy leaders to attract their people, intending good rather than contempt for the poor, but God forbade it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p158/r4.anchor: كان قد هم بتقديم الرؤساء وأولي الأموال على الضعفاء وذوي المسكنة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says calling on God morning and evening means performing the obligatory dawn and afternoon prayers; Hasan, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Dahhak similarly define it as prescribed prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r1.anchor: بالصلاة المكتوبة يعني: صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r2.speaker: إبراهيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r2.claim: Ibrahim offers remembrance of God at the two ends of the day as one meaning, but also reports that the phrase means the five obligatory prayers, as all exegetes hold.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r2.anchor: (الدعاء هاهنا الذكر، أي: يذكرون ربهم طرفي النهار)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r3.claim: Ibn Amir reads al-ghuduwa with waw; Abu Ali favors the common al-ghadāh because it can be indefinite and take the article, while ghuduwa is ordinarily a definite proper time-name.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r4.claim: Abu Ali says the manuscript's waw does not establish that reading, since ṣalāh is also written with waw for alif; Sibawayh treats ghuduwa and bukra as names for times, with Yūnus reporting their definite use without nunation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r4.anchor: وإن كانت قد كتبت في المصحف بالواو لم تدل على ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r5.claim: For Ibn Amir's reading, Abu Ali cites al-Khalil's permission to say 'today, ghuduwa and bukra' like ḍaḥwa, and time-names sometimes take the article when construed as generic.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r5.anchor: زعم الخليل أنه يجوز أن يقول: أتيتك اليوم غدوة وبكرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r6.claim: The author explains that a proper name becomes shareable and generic when stripped of its individual reference, making forms such as 'the Zayds' possible; the discussion cites Ibn Mayada.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p162/r6.anchor: فإذا شورك في اسمه فقد خرج عن أن يكون علما معروفا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the poor worshippers seek God's reward and act for His pleasure without associating anything with Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r1.anchor: يطلبون ثواب الله ويعملون ابتغاء مرضاة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r2.claim: One interpretation takes 'His face' as God's obedience and the direction or path He commanded people to follow; al-Zajjaj says it testifies to sincere intentions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r3.claim: The other interpretation uses 'face' as an honorific expression: they seek God alone; Abu Ishaq gives this explanation at 18:28.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p167/r3.anchor: يريدونه إلا أنه يؤتى بلفظ الوجه للتعظيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the reckoning pronouns to refer to the polytheists: the Prophet is not accountable for them, nor they for him; God alone rewards His allies and punishes His enemies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r1.anchor: ما عليك من حساب المشركين من شيء ولا على المشركين من حسابك من شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r2.claim: On Ibn Abbas's reading, the Prophet must not court the polytheists by excluding poor believers; the believers' reward is not theirs to give.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r2.anchor: ليس ثوابك عليهم حتى تلين لهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r3.claim: Most exegetes take the pronouns to refer to the poor worshippers; this best fits the explicit object of 'expel them'.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r3.anchor: والمفسرون (¬1) يردون الكناية إلى {الذين يدعون ربهم} وهم الفقراء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r4.claim: One explanation says the Prophet is not responsible for their actions or account of their actions; Ibn Abbas also reports this meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r4.anchor: ما عليك من عملهم ومن حساب عملهم من شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r5.claim: The story resembles Noah's people calling his followers the lowly: the prophets defer their deeds and livelihood to God, and the poor believers' humble trades do not disgrace the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p168/r5.anchor: قال له قومه: {قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the repeated reckoning clause confirms parallel phrasing, though the second phrase could be omitted.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r2.claim: A second view concerns provision: neither the Prophet's nor the poor believers' livelihood depends on one another, because God provides for all; he should let them draw near.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r2.anchor: ليس رزقك عليهم ولا رزقهم عليك وإنما يرزقك وإياهم الله الرازق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r3.claim: The warning against becoming one of the wrongdoers means harming oneself through disobedience and losing reward; ظلم can mean diminution in Arabic and in Quranic usage.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd calls expelling the poor injustice to them: they did not deserve it, so the author calls this a sound interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p170/r4.anchor: إنهم لم يستحقوا منك الطرد فإذا طردتهم فقد ظلمتهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r1.claim: The verse concerns poor believers after Meccan chiefs told the Prophet to remove them so the chiefs could sit with him and believe.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r1.anchor: نزلت في فقراء المؤمنين لما قال رؤساء الكفار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r2.claim: Calling on God morning and evening means performing the obligatory prayers; seeking his face means seeking his reward.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r3.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for the poor people's provision, nor are they responsible for his; God provides for all, so he should keep them near.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r3.anchor: ليس رزقك عليهم، ولا رزقهم عليك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:52-53/r4.claim: Expelling these believers would wrong them.

ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r1.claim: The Prophet must not expel people who worship their Lord morning and evening, continually seeking God's presence and favor with sincere, exclusive devotion.
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r1.anchor: sabah akşam, yani her zaman Rablerine dua ve ibadet ederler

ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r2.claim: Neither their reckoning belongs to the Prophet nor his reckoning to them; he must not expel them on the pretext of accounting for them.
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r2.anchor: Onların hesaplarından hiçbir şey sana ait değil

ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r3.claim: Expelling these worshippers would make the Prophet one of the wrongdoers.

ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r4.claim: Elmalılı reports that Quraysh leaders asked Muhammad to remove poor Muslims such as Suhayb, Khabbāb, Bilāl, ʿAmmār, and Salmān so they might visit; after Umar urged trying it and they pressed for a written promise, the verse was revealed and the Prophet discarded the page.
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r4.anchor: Rivayet olunuyor ki Kureyş’in ileri gelenlerinden birtakımları Hazret-i Peygamber’e uğramışlar

ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r5.speaker: Selmân ve Habbâb
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r5.claim: Salmān and Khabbāb say the verse concerned them: the Prophet sat close with them and would not leave before they did; after 18:28, he stayed with them and thanked God for the command.

ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r6.claim: God tests one group through another: arrogant elites scorn poor, sincere believers as undeserving, while faith and sincerity are divine gifts that challenge worldly pride and status.
ELMALILI:6:50-55#2/r6.anchor: bir fitne ile yani tard ü istihkāra şâyan zannedilen fukara ve zu‘afâyı iman ve ihlâs ile memnun ve muazzez etmek gibi bir imtihan iledir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r1.claim: A report in Muslim and other hadith collections says Quraysh notables demanded the poor, vulnerable Companions leave before they would meet Muhammad; he refused, then considered their lesser demand before this verse stopped him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r1.anchor: Müslim’in Sahîh’i (“Fezâilü’s-sahâbe”, 45-46) ve diğer bazı hadis kaynaklarında yer alan bir rivayete göre

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r2.speaker: müfessirlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r2.claim: Most commentators, noting reports that the whole surah descended at once rather than in parts, deny that this verse was occasioned by that incident; even if so, the incident only occasions its universal ethical teaching.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r2.anchor: müfessirlerin çoğu bu sûrenin, parça parça değil, tamamının bir defada indiğini bildiren haberleri de dikkate alarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r3.speaker: some interpreters
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r3.claim: Some interpreters take the pronoun ‘they’ in the accountability clause to refer to the polytheists.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r3.anchor: “Onların hesaplarından sana sorumluluk yoktur...” cümlesindeki “onlar” zamiriyle müşriklere işaret edildiğini düşünenler olmuşsa da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r4.speaker: ağırlıklı görüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r4.claim: The predominant view is that ‘they’ refers to the poor Muslims mentioned earlier.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r4.anchor: ağırlıklı görüş, bununla yukarıda anılan müslümanların kastedildiği yönündedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r5.speaker: müşrikler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r5.claim: The polytheists alleged that the poor Muslims gathered around the Prophet for shelter, food, and drink rather than sincere devotion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r5.anchor: Rivayete göre müşrikler, Hz. Peygamber’in çevresinde toplanan söz konusu kişilerin, aslında –samimi dindarlıklarından değil– barınma imkânı buldukları, yiyip içtikleri için orada toplandıklarını ileri sürmüşlerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r6.speaker: one view
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r6.claim: One interpretation says the verse separates the Prophet’s responsibility from the poor Muslims’ responsibility: each bears their own deeds, so he should remain close to them rather than wrong them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r6.anchor: herkesin kendi yapıp ettiklerinin sorumluluğunu yine kendisinin taşıdığı bildirilerek Resûl-i Ekrem’in onlara olan ilgisini sürdürmesi istenmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r7.speaker: another interpretation
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r7.claim: Another reading says the Prophet should not send worshipping poor people away to earn a living: their provision is God’s responsibility, not his calculation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r7.anchor: herkesin rızkını verenin Allah Teâlâ olduğuna işaret buyurulmuştur (Râzî, XII, 236-237)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r8.claim: Human worth in Islam rests on faith, reverence for God, and spiritual nobility rather than rank, wealth, or lineage; the verse also shows the Prophet’s character formed by Qur’anic principles.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r8.anchor: mevki, zenginlik ve soyuna göre değil iman zenginliğine, Allah’a saygı ve ruh yüceliğine göre değer taşıdığını ortaya koyması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r9.claim: Humiliating people valued by God for faith and conduct is injustice, even if the hypothetical offender were a prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r9.anchor: farzımuhal bu kimse peygamber bile olsa– zalim olarak gösterilmesi son derece ilgi çekicidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r10.speaker: Habbâb
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r10.claim: After the verse, the Prophet and poor Muslims grew so close that they sat knee to knee, and he waited for them to rise before leaving so as not to hurt them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:52/r10.anchor: Habbâb’ın anlattığına göre bu âyetin inmesinden sonra Hz. Peygamber’le yoksul ve kimsesiz müslümanlar arasındaki yakınlık o kadar artmıştır

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r1.speaker: خباب
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that Aqra ibn Habis and Uyayna ibn Hisn asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers such as Suhayb, Bilal, Ammar, and Khabbab when Arab delegations arrived; the verse forbidding their expulsion was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r1.anchor: جاء الأقرع ابن حابس وعيينة بن حصن فوجدا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع صهيب وبلال وعمار وخباب قاعدا في ناس من الضعفاء

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report unusual because the verse is Meccan while Aqra and Uyayna converted much later, after the Hijra.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p101/r3.anchor: قال ابن كثير هذا حديث غريب فإن الآية مكية والأقرع وعيينة إنما أسلما بعد الهجرة بدهر

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r4.speaker: سعد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r4.claim: Saʿd says the verse was revealed about six poor companions—himself, Ibn Masʿūd, Ṣuhayb, ʿAmmār, al-Miqdād, and Bilāl—after Quraysh demanded their expulsion.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r4.anchor: عن المقدام بن شريح عن أبيه عن سعد قال: نزلت هذه الآية فينا ستة في وفي ابن مسعود وصهيب وعمار والمقداد وبلال

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r5.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r5.claim: Khabbāb says the verse concerned weak companions who sat with the Prophet morning and evening to learn the Qur’an and religion and hear about Paradise, Hell, death, and resurrection.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p216/r5.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: فينا نزلت، كنا ضعفاء عند النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالغداة والعشي، فعلمنا القرآن والخير

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r1.speaker: الأقرع بن حابس وعيينة بن حصن
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r1.claim: Al-Aqraʿ b. Ḥābis and ʿUyayna b. Ḥiṣn demanded that the Prophet expel the poor companions before they would sit with him; the verses were revealed in response.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r1.anchor: فجاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي وعيينة بن حصن الفزاري فقالا: إنا من أشراف قومنا وإنا نكره أن يرونا معهم فاطردهم إذا جالسناك

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r2.speaker: ابن مسعد
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Quraysh leaders objected to the Prophet’s companions Khabbāb, Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and ʿAmmār, asking whether they were to become their followers.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعد قال: مر الملأ من قريش على رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وعنده خباب بن الأرت وصهيب وبلال وعمار

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r3.speaker: الربيع
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says poor companions, including Bilāl, ʿAmmār, Ṣuhayb, and Salmān, took the Prophet’s seats first; nobles asked him to draw them near, and the verse followed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r3.anchor: عن الربيع قال: كان رجال يسبقون إلى مجلس رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ومنهم بلال وعمار وصهيب وسلمان

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r4.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r4.claim: ʿIkrima reports that Banū ʿAbd Manāf’s chiefs asked Abū Ṭālib to have Muhammad dismiss his freedmen, servants, and poor followers; ʿUmar suggested trying this, and apologized after revelation.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p217/r4.anchor: قال عكرمة: جاء عتبة بن ربيعة وشيبة بن ربيعة ومطعم بن عدي والحارث بن نوفل في أشراف بني عبد مناف

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p37/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p37/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p37/.claim: The Prophet is not accountable for arrogant people’s refusal, and neither are they accountable for his duties in a way that could justify his turning believers away; doing so would be injustice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p37/.anchor: Similarly, these people will not be held responsible on the Day of Judgement for the duties imposed on him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p38/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p38/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p38/.claim: Muhammad must not abandon sincere worshippers to appease wealthy, arrogant people who disparage his poor companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p38/.anchor: he should not waste any more time on the wretched among them who are inebriated by their status

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.claim: Quraysh leaders disparaged the companions as poor menial workers and argued that respectable people could not join a religion that welcomed them; Muhammad must not lose true companions to win these elites.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.anchor: his companions were all poor who did menial jobs and how could God select such lowly sections of the society for His religion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.claim: If the elites persist in error, they alone bear its consequence; turning away genuine seekers would leave the Prophet liable for neglecting those deserving his care.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.anchor: If he goes after these wretched elements, they will not be held responsible on his behalf

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.claim: Addressing Muhammad rather than the Quraysh directly strikes at their arrogance and implies they are unworthy of direct address.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.anchor: instead of addressing them, the Prophet (sws) is addressed. This is to make evident to them that they are not even worthy of being addressed directly.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.claim: The verb used for driving the poor away is harsh and means to disregard someone disparagingly, matching what Quraysh wanted Muhammad to do to his companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.anchor: it means to disparagingly disregard someone.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.speaker: Jesus (sws)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.claim: Jesus’ lost-sheep parable depicts a shepherd seeking one straying sheep instead of being content with the ninety-nine.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.anchor: Jesus (sws) has stated a parable also: “What do you think? If a man owns a hundred sheep

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.claim: The lost-sheep parable illustrates God’s affection for people who return after error and a prophet’s concern for his nation’s faith.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p39/.anchor: Just as this parable shows the great affection God has for people who turn to Him after being in error

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.claim: Prophetic concern for people reflects God’s affection and is praiseworthy, but it has limits: the Prophet must not pursue the wayward at the expense of loyal companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.anchor: God does not want his prophet to go after those people who have gone astray at the expense of his real companions.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.claim: Farāhī discusses important points on this topic in his commentary on Sūrah ‘Abas; Islahi says he will give his own view later.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p40/.anchor: Ustādh Far āhī has written some very important points related to this topic in his exegesis of Sūrah ‘Abas.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p41/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p41/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p41/.claim: The poor believers seek only their Creator’s pleasure, so the promised mercy and forgiveness answer their actual desire rather than worldly status or riches.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p41/.anchor: The only desire they had was to please their creator and master.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p257/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p257/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p257/r4.claim: Ibn Amir alone reads بالغدوة with wāw throughout the Quran; the others have alif.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p257/r4.anchor: كلهم قرأ ﴿ بالغداة ﴾ بألف إلا ابن عامر فإنه قرأ / بالغدوة / فى كل القرآن بالواو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r1.claim: Their invocation publicly professed faith in God alone, implying conviction; hypocrisy had not appeared before the community in Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r1.anchor: ومعنى { يدعون ربهم } يعلنون إيمانهم به دون الأصنام إعلانا بالقول ، وهو يستلزم اعتقاد القائل بما يقوله ، إذ لم يكن يومئذ نفاق وإنما ظهر المنافقون بالمدينة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r2.claim: Al-ghadāh is early morning and al-ʿashiyy spans noon to dawn; the generic terms and temporal bāʾ mean they invoke God throughout the day and all days.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r2.anchor: والمعنى أنهم يدعون الله اليوم كله . فالغداة والعشي قصد بهما استيعاب الزمان والأيام كما يقصد بالمشرق والمغرب استيعاب الأمكنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r3.claim: An alternative takes invocation as prayer and morning and evening as all times of the five daily prayers, so the prohibition means not to expel worshippers, that is, believers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r3.anchor: وقيل : أريد بالدعاء الصلاة . وبالغداة والعشي عموم أوقات الصلوات الخمس . فالمعنى ولا تطرد المصلين ، أي المؤمنين .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r4.claim: Most readers pronounce al-ghadāh with an open ghayn and long ā; Ibn ʿĀmir reads a rounded ghayn, silent dāl, and long wāw, a dialect form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { بالغداة } بفتح الغين وبألف بعد الدال . وقرأه ابن عامر بضم الغين وسكون الدال وبواو ساكنة بعد الدال وهي لغة في الغداة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r5.claim: The clause about seeking His face is circumstantial and means they invoke God sincerely for His pleasure, seeking no worldly advantage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r5.anchor: وجملة { يريدون وجهه } حال من الضمير المرفوع في { يدعون } ، أي يدعون مخلصين يريدون وجه الله ، أي لا يريدون حظا دنيويا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r6.claim: Face literally names the part of the head with the sensory organs and can stand metonymically for the whole essence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r6.anchor: والوجه حقيقة الجزء من الرأس الذي فيه العينان والأنف والفم . ويطلق الوجه على الذات كلها مجازا مرسلا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r7.claim: Here face is a metaphor for the essence, with an implicit modifier; the meaning is seeking God’s pleasure rather than pleasing anyone else.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r7.anchor: والوجه هنا مستعار للذات على اعتبار مضاف ، أي يريدون رضى الله ، أي لا يريدون إرضاء غيره .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r8.claim: Although it was said that Quraysh accused poor believers of hypocrisy, no sound report supports this; the phrase most likely praises their complete faith rather than answering that accusation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r8.anchor: وقد قيل : إن قريشا طعنوا في إيمان الضعفاء ونسبوهم إلى النفاق ، إلا أن هذا لم يرد به أثر صحيح ، فالأظهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r9.claim: The following clause may explain why the believers must not be expelled or invalidate the rationale for seeking their expulsion; since invalidating the forbidden act’s rationale becomes a reason for the prohibition, the sentence is separated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p247/r9.anchor: وجملة { ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء } تعليل للنهي عن طردهم ، أو إبطال لعلة الهم بطردهم ، أو لعلة طلب طردهم . فإن إبطال علة فعل المنهي عنه يؤول إلى كونه تعليلا للنهي ، ولذا فصلت هذه الجملة .

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: The pattern فَعول can form verbal nouns, but the same surface form may instead denote an amount, result, agent, patient, or a related noun; these meanings must be learned lexically.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: وذلك قولك توضأت وضوءا حسنا وأولعت به ولوعا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: وقود can refer to the act of burning or to fuel; the form with fatḥa is the more common word for firewood, while قبولا is also attested.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: وقدت النار وقودا عاليا وقبله قبولا والوقود أكثر والوقود الحطب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: شبعه and ملء can mean the amount that satisfies or fills, unlike شبعا and ملئا when they denote the acts; طعم may likewise mean flavor or the act of tasting.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: شبعه وهذا شبعه إنما يريد قدر ما

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: Some forms do not differ from their verbal nouns in meaning, as in رويت ريا, أصاب ريه, طعمت طعما, نهل نهلا, and أصاب نهله.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: These patterns are not fully predictable: خرص, الكيلة, قوت, and الحلب can vary in form and meaning, and الحلب may mean the milk as well as the act of milking.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: فهذه أشياء تجيء مختلفة ولا تطرد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: مرية denotes an amount of milk rather than the act; لعنة may name the cursed person, and الخلق may mean the created thing rather than creation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: وقالوا لعنة للذي يلعن واللعنة المصدر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: كرع is the water one drinks from; ذو تدرإ means a person with means or protection, not the act of driving away, and لعنة can mean a person notorious for cursing.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: Forms on مفعول can denote a passive result: لبن حلب is milked milk, الخلق is the created thing, and ضرب الأمير is coin struck by the emir.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: على المفعول وذلك قولك لبن حلب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: Some forms denote an agent: يوم غم means a cloudy day and رجل نوم a sleeping man.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: ويقع على الفاعل وذلك قولك يوم غم ورجل نوم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: صرى describes milk that has lightly changed in the udder; معشر كرم is likewise used with the sense of approved or pleasing.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: كما يقولون هو رضا إنما يريدون المرضي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.claim: A singular member of a collective can take the collective’s pattern with feminine ة, as in بيض/بيضة, جوز/جوزة, شمط/شمطة, and شيب/شيبة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالمصادرعلىفعول)#6.anchor: كما قالوا بيض وبيضة وجوز وجوزة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.claim: Sibawayh reports that al-Khalīl and Abū al-Khaṭṭāb attribute this rare Fuzāra and some-Qays dialect: final alif becomes yāʾ in pause and returns to alif in connection.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.anchor: وذلك قول بعض العرب في أفعى هذه أفعى وفي حبلى هذه حبلى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.claim: Sibawayh prefers the familiar majority pronunciation: retain final alif in pause; it converges with the rare form in connected speech, where alif is clearer.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.anchor: الألف في الوقف على حالها ولا تبدلها ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.speaker: طيء
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.claim: Tayyiʾ speakers keep final alif in both pause and liaison because it is faint, unchanging, and close to hamza.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.anchor: وأما طيء فزعموا أنهم يدعونها في الوصل على حالها في الوقف لأنها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.speaker: بعض طيئ
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.claim: Some Tayyiʾ speakers choose wāw instead, saying أفعو because it is clearer than yāʾ and resembles alif in openness and length.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.anchor: وزعموا أن بعض طيئ يقول أفعو لأنها أبين من الياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.speaker: بنو تميم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.claim: Banū Tamīm say هذه at pause but هذي فلانة in connection; yāʾ and its kasra become especially faint at pause, so they replace them with a clearer nearby sound.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.anchor: بني تميم في الوقف هذه فإذا وصلوا قالوا هذي فلانة لأن الياء خفية

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.speaker: أهل الحجاز وغيرهم من قيس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.claim: The people of the Hijaz and others of Qays use hāʾ in pause and connection, unlike Tayyiʾ's yāʾ; this is exceptional, not a general rule for every yāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.anchor: وأما أهل الحجاز وغيرهم من قيس فألزموها الهاء في

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.speaker: ناس من بني سعد
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.claim: Banū Saʿd replace weak final yāʾ with clearer jīm at pause (تميمج, علج, عربانج); an unattributed line uses بالعشج for بالعشي and البرنج for البرني.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالحرفالذيتبدلمكانهفيالوق.anchor: وأما ناس من بني سعد فإنهم يبدلون الجيم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: Root-initial yāʾ is not treated like wāw in these forms because it is lighter and closer to alif; forms such as يئس and يبس retain it.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: نحو عاود وطاول وذلك قولهم يئس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: Sibawayh's evidence is that speakers retain root yāʾ in ييئس and ييبس, unlike deletion in يعد; the broken plural also gives يوابس.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: ويدلك على أن الياء أخف عليهم من الواو أنهم يقولون ييئس وييبس فلا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: When root-initial yāʾ is quiescent after ḍamma, it shifts to wāw, as in موقن, موسر, موئس, and مويس; Sibawayh also compares the reverse shift in ميزان.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: وقبلها ضمة قلبتها واوا كما قلبت الواو ياء في ميزان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: Some speakers say يا زيد يئس, analogizing it to قيل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم يا زيد يئس شبهها بقيل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: أبو عمرو
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: Abū ʿAmr's reading يا صالحيتنا turns hamza into yāʾ but does not further change it to wāw.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: أبا عمرو قرأ يا صالحيتنا جعل الهمزة ياء ثم لم يقلبها واوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: Sibawayh calls this a weak language when the following word is not separate; the predicted but unattested form would be يا غلاموجل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: هذه لغة ضعيفة لأن قياس هذا أن تقول يا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: In iftiʿāl forms, initial yāʾ becomes tāʾ, as in اتبس, since it can weaken and is a counterpart of wāw.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: والياء توافق الواو في افتعل في أنك تقلب الياء تاء في افتعل من

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: The afʿal pattern generally preserves initial yāʾ because it also preserves wāw, except for isolated irregular forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: فأما أفعل فإنها تسلم لأن الواو تسلم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: Forms such as يا تئس and يا تبس use tāʾ analogically, but Sibawayh says this cause is not productive beyond the specified cases and isolated anomalies.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: وقد قالوا يا تئس ويا تبس فجعلوها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.claim: Sibawayh treats يبس يابس like يئس, analogizing them to يعد; the analogy is limited to those lexical cases.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماكانتالياءفيهأولاوكانتف.anchor: قالوا يبس يابس كما قالوا يئس يئس فشبهوها بيعد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: In forms such as غارت غوورا and القوول, wāw may be lengthened or hamzaed; hamza occurs where wāw meets ḍamma, whose sound is less distinct.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: وقد همزوا كما همزوا أدؤر لاجتماع الواو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The same change is not made to yāʾ in these patterns because yāʾ is lighter and resembles alif, though it does shift to yāʾ in the pattern فعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: ولا يفعلون ذلك بالياء في هذه الأبنية لأنها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: In فعل, wāw shifts to yāʾ after ḍamma in صوم→صيم, قوم→قيم, قول→قيل, and نوم→نيم, by analogy with forms such as عتي and جثي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: في فعل وذلك قولهم صيم في صوم وقيم في قوم وقيل في قول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The wāw remains in زوار and صوام because distance from the word's end strengthens it; the change is regular in فعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: زوار وصوام لأنهم شبهوا الواو في صيم بها في عتو إذا كانت لاما وقبل اللام

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: Forms such as مشوب/مشيب and حور/حير are analogized to فعل and follow its alternation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: مشوب ومشيب وحور وحير وهذا النحو فشبهوه بفعل وأجروه مجراه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: طويل and طوال preserve the original wāw, like جاور and جوار, because the singular retains the original form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: طوال فهو بمنزلة جاور وجوار لأنها حية في الواحد على الأصل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: Fʿlān and fʿlā generally retain original wāw as augmented nouns analogize to unaugmented patterns; Sibawayh says weak-root forms such as غزوان and نزوان avoid this unchanged outcome.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: فيجري على الأصل وفعلى نحو جولان وحيدان وصورى وحيدى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The pattern فعلاء likewise stays on the original form, with السيراء, قوباء, خيلاء, and عرواء as examples.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: السيراء وفعلاء بمنزلة ذلك قالوا قوباء وخيلاء فتمت كما قالوا عرواء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: Some speakers also apply the فعل alternation to فعلان and فعلى, treating the suffix as if it were feminine tāʾ; Sibawayh says this is not regular, citing داران, حادان, هامان, and دالان.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: قال بعضهم في فعلان وفعلى كما قالوا في فعل ولا زيادة فيه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: Other forms of فعلى and the related pattern do not undergo this sound change, just as فعل and فعل do not.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: وأما فعلى وفعلى وهذا النحو فلا تدخله العلة

IBNMAJAH:4127/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:4127/r1.speaker: خباب
IBNMAJAH:4127/r1.claim: Khabbāb reports al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna sought private access and asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers; Gabriel revealed 6:52 against this, while 6:53–54 and 18:28 reinforce God's favor and companionship with sincere believers.
IBNMAJAH:4127/r1.anchor: عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى ‏{وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ

SULAMI:v1p21/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p21/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
SULAMI:v1p21/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd says the Qur'an came in seven modes, every verse has an outward and inward sense, and every letter has a limit and an opening; it supplies a layered-reading framework.
SULAMI:v1p21/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ' إن القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف

SULAMI:v1p21/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p21/r2.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SULAMI:v1p21/r2.claim: Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad divides the Book into worship, allusion, subtleties, and realities, respectively suited to ordinary people, the elect, saints, and prophets.
SULAMI:v1p21/r2.anchor: وحكى عن جعفر بن محمد أنه قال : كتاب الله على أربعة أشياء : العبادة والإشارة

SULAMI:v1p21/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p21/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
SULAMI:v1p21/r3.claim: ʿAlī says each verse has four senses: outward recitation, inward understanding, a limit comprising expression, allusion and lawful/unlawful rulings, and an opening that is God's intent for His servants.
SULAMI:v1p21/r3.anchor: وقال على بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه : ما من آية إلا ولها أربعة معان : ظاهر وباطن وحد ومطلع

SULAMI:v1p21/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p21/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
SULAMI:v1p21/r4.claim: ʿAlī maps worship to hearing, allusion to reason, subtleties to witnessing, and realities to surrender.
SULAMI:v1p21/r4.anchor: فالعبادة للسمع والإشارة للعقل واللطائف للمشاهدة والحقائق للاستسلام

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r14.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r14.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r14.claim: In 6:52, وجهه is an added expression meaning that they seek God through supplication.

IBNHISHAM:v1p392#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p392#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p392#2/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that Quraysh mocked the Prophet’s poor companions—Khabbāb, ʿAmmār, Abū Fākihah Yasār, Suhayb, and others—saying they should not have received guidance first; verses 6:52–54 were revealed in response.
IBNHISHAM:v1p392#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا جلس في المسجد، فجلس إليه المستضعفون من أصحابه

BURHAN:v3p461/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p461/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p461/r3.claim: The verse interweaves two premise–consequence pairs: the warning against expulsion leads to not becoming wrongdoers, while the reciprocal accounting clauses lead to the question of expelling them.

BURHAN:v3p292#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p292#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p292#2/r1.claim: The author defines inversion as a verbal figure and gives reciprocal formulations: account is not yours/theirs, wives are each other's garment, neither is lawful to the other, and night and day enter one another.
BURHAN:v3p292#2/r1.anchor: العكس وهو أمر لفظي كقوله ﴿ ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء وما من حسابك عليهم من شيء ﴾

ITQAN:v4p397/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p397/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p397/r11.claim: Those who call on their Lord morning and evening include Suhayb, Bilal, Ammar, Khabbab, Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, Ibn Masud, and Salman al-Farisi.
ITQAN:v4p397/r11.anchor: سمي منهم صهيب وبلال وعمار وخباب وسعد بن أبي وقاص وابن مسعود وسلمان الفارسي

ITQAN:v3p249/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p249/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p249/r1.claim: Aks reverses the parts of a statement in its second half; examples include the mirrored clauses in 6:52 and other paired Quranic formulations.
ITQAN:v3p249/r1.anchor: هو أن يؤتى بكلام يقدم فيه جزء ويؤخر آخر ثم يقدم المؤخر ويؤخر المقدم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r1.claim: Word order should not be divided into cases where it carries meaning and cases where it is mere poetic license; a placement that adds a benefit does so consistently.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r1.anchor: واعلم أن من الخطأ أن يقسم الأمر في تقديم الشيء وتأخيره قسمين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r2.claim: With hamza questions, verb-first أفعلت asks whether the act occurred, while noun-first أأنت فعلت asks who performed it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p99/r2.anchor: إذا قلت : أفعلت ؟ فبدأت بالفعل كان الشك في الفعل نفسه

DAMGHANI:v1p481/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p481/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p481/r7.claim: In 6:52, “seeking His face” means seeking God and His pleasure; the other cited uses of face likewise mean God.
DAMGHANI:v1p481/r7.anchor: الثالث وجهه يعني الله ورضاه قوله تعالى في سورة الأنعام ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي يريدون وجهه يعني يريدون الله تعالى ورضاه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r1.claim: The basic meaning of وجه is an animal's face; it is named for the usual occurrence of facing through it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r1.anchor: الوجه : في الأصل اسم للعضو المخصوص في الحيوان . وسمي وجها لأن المواجهة تقع به في غالب الحال

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r2.claim: By extension, وجه can mean the aspect selected over others, the leader or front of something, or the beginning of the day.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r2.anchor: ثم يستعار ذلك في كل ما يراد تقديمه على ما سواه . فيقال : هذا وجه الرأي ، وهذا وجه القوم ومستقبل كل شيء : وجهه . ووجه النهار : أوله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj cites a poem using بوجه نهار to show that وجه النهار means the beginning of the day.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r3.anchor: ووجه النهار : أوله . وأنشد الزجاج في ذلك : من كان مسرورا بمقتل مالك … فليأت نسوتنا بوجه نهار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r6.claim: In 6:52, وجهه means God's own self; the source groups several other verses with this sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r6.anchor: والثالث : الذات . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

IBNMAJAH:4128/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:4128/r1.speaker: سعد
IBNMAJAH:4128/r1.claim: Saʿd reports that this verse was revealed about six believers, including him, Ibn Masʿud, Suhayb, ʿAmmar, al-Miqdad and Bilal, after Quraysh demanded that they be sent away.
IBNMAJAH:4128/r1.anchor: عَنْ سَعْدٍ، قَالَ نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ فِينَا سِتَّةٍ فِيَّ وَفِي ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ

MUSLIM:6241/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:6241/r1.speaker: سعد
MUSLIM:6241/r1.claim: Saʿd reports that the polytheists demanded the Prophet expel six poor companions, including Saʿd, Ibn Masʿud, and Bilal; the verse forbidding their dismissal was then revealed.
MUSLIM:6241/r1.anchor: عَنْ سَعْدٍ، قَالَ كُنَّا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم سِتَّةَ نَفَرٍ فَقَالَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ لِلنَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم اطْرُدْ هَؤُلاَءِ لاَ يَجْتَرِئُونَ عَلَيْنَا

ITQAN:v3p16/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p16/r7.speaker: ابن اللبان
ITQAN:v3p16/r7.claim: Ibn al-Labbān interprets God's face in these expressions as sincerity of intention, including feeding for God's sake and seeking the Lord's face.
ITQAN:v3p16/r7.anchor: وقال ابن اللبان في قوله ﴿ يريدون وجهه ﴾ ﴿ إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله ﴾

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: Weak wāw in verbal nouns such as حيالا and قياما becomes yāʾ when flanked by kasra and a following yāʾ-like vowel, matching the weak verb.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: وذلك قولك حالت حيالا وقمت قياما وإنما قلبوها حيث كانت معتلة في الفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: In plurals such as سوط/سياط, ثوب/ثياب, and روضة/رياض, dormant wāw after kasra changes by analogy with يقول; the following alif acts like yāʾ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: ميتة ساكنة شبهوها بواو يقول لأنها ساكنة مثلها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: A yāʾ already substituted for wāw in the singular is kept in the plural after kasra, as in ديمة/ديم and دار/ديار; this is likelier after alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: وذلك قولهم ديمة وديم وقامة وقيم وتارة وتير ودار وديار

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: When the singular keeps wāw and no alif follows, the plural retains it, as in حول and عوض, and in كوز/كوزة and related forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: كما قلت فعل فأثبت ذلك وذلك قولك حول وعوض

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: ثورة/ثيرة shows a change after kasra, but Sibawayh says the pattern is not productive.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: وقد قالوا ثورة وثيرة قلبوها حيث كانت بعد كسرة واستثقلوا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The plural أقوال keeps wāw in قيل/قول because no preceding kasra or yāʾ makes it heavy.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: أقوال لأنه ليس قبلها ما يستثقل معه من كسرة أو ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: In broken plurals, خيانة and حياكة become خوائن and حوائك: wāw after fatḥa is lighter, and after alif it follows the pattern of عاود.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: قلت رسالة ورسائل لقلت حوائك وخوائن لأن الواو إذا كانت بعد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: Forms such as اجتاز/اجتيازا and انقاد/انقيادا change wāw to yāʾ between kasra and alif; unlike الإقامة, the preceding consonant was not originally still.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: ومما أجرى مجرى حالت حيالا ونامت نياما اجتزت اجتيازا وانقدت انقيادا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The verbal nouns of اختار/اختير and انقاد/انقيد pattern with قال/قيل in their weakness.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: فأما اسم اختار واختير فمعتل كما اعتل اسم قال

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: الفعال forms الجوار and الحوار retain their original wāw because their verbs are sound, like تجاور and التجاور.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: وذلك الجوار والحوار ومثل ذلك عاونته عوانا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: In فعول, wāw is not preceded by kasra and remains original; wāw may also be hamzated after ḍamma, with both options regular.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: فليس قبل الواو فيه كسرة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: These patterns do not make the same change to yāʾ, which is lighter; still, yāʾ may replace wāw in فعل forms such as صيم and قيل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: ولا يفعلون ذلك بالياء في هذه الأبنية لأنها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: In فعل, forms such as صوم/صيم, قول/قيل, and نوم/نيم show yāʾ replacing wāw by analogy with عتو/عتي.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: صيم في صوم وقيم في قوم وقيل في قول ونيم في نوم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The change is absent in زوار and صوام: the more distant wāw is likened to root-final wāw, weakening the analogy.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: زوار وصوام لأنهم شبهوا الواو في صيم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: مشوب/مشيب and حور/حير follow the same analogy with فعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: مشوب ومشيب وحور وحير وهذا النحو

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: طويل/طوال behaves like جاور/جوار because wāw remains active in the singular.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: وطوال فهو بمنزلة جاور وجوار لأنها حية

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: فعلان and فعلى generally retain original wāw, as in جولان, حيدان, صورى, and حيدى, because augmentation makes them resemble unaugmented nouns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: فعلى نحو جولان وحيدان وصورى وحيدى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The original form is not used in weaker defective cases such as غزوان and نزوان, unlike the stronger defective patterns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: نحو غزوان ونزوان ونفيان ويتركان في المعتل الأقوى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The same original-vowel treatment occurs in فعلاء, including قوباء and خيلاء.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: قالوا قوباء وخيلاء فتمت كما قالوا عرواء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: Some speakers extend the فعل pattern to فعلان and فعلى, treating the added ending like tāʾ marbūṭa; forms such as داران and حادان result, but the pattern is irregular.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.anchor: قال بعضهم في فعلان وفعلى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتقلبالواوفيهياءلالياءقبل.claim: The remaining stated فعلى categories do not undergo this weak-letter rule, just as فعل and فعل do not.
